html:
A pyramid-shaped mud-brick tower about 17 metres high in Gao, built by Askia Muhammad I on his return from the pilgrimage to Mecca in 1495, which became his tomb.

Askia Muhammad made the Songhai Empire the largest state of West Africa and promoted Islam and learning. The tomb, with its mosque and courtyard, is the finest example of the Sahel building style that spread from Mali to Niger. Gao, on the Niger, was Songhai's capital until the Moroccan invasion of 1591. UNESCO listed the tomb in 2004; since the Mali War it has been on the list of heritage in danger. See also Timbuktu.
